transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello, Mrs. Al-Rashid. I wanted to come by and talk with you about what happened in the holding area before your procedure.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Hello, Doctor.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it was a very stressful start to your morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I was... I was very surprised.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is completely understandable that you felt shocked. I can only imagine how unsettling it was to see the mark on the wrong side of your body.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just thought... I thought perhaps I had misunderstood where the lesion was.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, you were absolutely correct. The wrong site was marked for the excision. We marked your left arm when the procedure was supposed to be on your right arm.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I have never seen this happen.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Does that explanation make sense to you, or can I clarify anything about how the marking happened?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No, I understand. But how could this happen in a hospital?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a failure in our process. The marking was done incorrectly during the pre-operative check, and we didn't catch it until you spoke up.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I felt very bad pointing it out to the nurse. I did not want to be rude.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You were not being rude at all. In fact, your alertness is what ensured the procedure happened on the correct side.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But I thought the doctors always knew.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a very frightening feeling when the person you trust makes a mistake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am just glad you found it before the surgery started.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, it is fortunate that it was caught in time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is this something that happens often here?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is rare, but it is something we take very seriously.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I see.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to make sure you feel okay about moving forward with the recovery of the actual site.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am fine, thank you. I just feel a bit shaken.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is a very normal reaction to this kind of situation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will there be a report?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There will be an internal review of the event.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I hope it helps other people.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It will.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happens now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will continue to monitor your incision today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll check in on you again tomorrow morning before I leave for the day to see how the healing is progressing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you, Doctor.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You're welcome.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Should I tell my daughter about this when she visits?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is entirely up to you, but we are happy to discuss it with her if you would like us to be there.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Maybe later.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Of course. I'll let you get some rest now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll be back in a few hours to check your dressing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, alright.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Rest well.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Goodbye.

H.justification: Resident allows full pauses, never interrupts, and uses no rushing language throughout the interaction.

E.justification: Error named explicitly in the second turn, lay language used, and comprehension checked twice ('Does that explanation make sense', 'can I clarify').

A.justification: No direct apology language such as 'I'm sorry' or 'I apologize' is used in the transcript.

R.justification: Specific emotions are named back ('shocked', 'frightening feeling', 'normal reaction') and the resident engages the patient's emotional bids regarding her alertness and fear.

T.justification: Specific next steps and timelines are provided (monitoring today, check tomorrow), but there is no named patient role or discussion of prevention.
